chapter: Sue and Patsy Howard in show business
title: The WPA Hot Mikado and Janet Collins
summary: Patsy describes the WPA production Hot Mikado, assistant choreography and ballerina Janet Collins.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That was in the thirties, '38 or '39, something like that. And as I said, when they had the WPA, they wanted to put on Hot Mikado and of course, they had to put the girls in the WPA in order to have a show, because at that time they only had like laborers.
There were no women in the WPA.

Only like those that could -- they had a few singers, like choirs and maybe seamstress and things like that, so when they wanted to do their show, they had to take all the girls that could dance and put them into the WPA. And they only got just one salary, everybody, which was 94-something a month. You know, they paid off by the month at that time. And Janet Collins, who was -- she was a beautiful ballerina, she was in that. We had a -- I did assistant
* Works Progress Administration, a New Deal program.
How long did that play run?
It ran about three months, I imagine.
Did you continue to work together, the same dancers.
Where did you go after that?
Well, probably into a club or something. I can't recall.
Did you work with Janet Collins long.
Just for that show. She was a marvelous dancer. Ballerina, rather.
She later became a ballerina with the Metropolitan Opera.
Right. Also her -- I think her niece, Carmen Delavallade, who is married to Jeffrey Holder, she also became -- at New York.
